title: RBAC v2 change trace: compact indexing & retention orchestration
creator: Ayesha Patel
description: Goal: ensure RBAC v2 role changes and admin actions are retained in a cost-controlled audit store with compacted indexing for fast change-trace queries. Scope includes ingest enrichment for RBAC delta events, a compact index schema that stores the latest effective state per subject+resource, partitioning and lifecycle rules (hot/warm/cold), and orchestration for tiered retention + automated compaction jobs. This ticket covers design, small PoC for compaction, and an initial rollout on non-prod namespaces.
acceptance_criteria: Ingest pipeline attaches rbac_v2.delta metadata (actor_id, actor_role_snapshot, change_type, txn_id) to audit events for all RBAC-related API paths.
Compact index schema implemented: single doc per org:subject:resource with last_seen_ts, last_change_txn, and a short change history (3 entries) for forensic queries.

Partitioning policy created and enforced: daily partitions for 30 days (hot), weekly partitions for 90 days (warm), monthly partitions for 2 years (cold) with configurable TTLs and cloud lifecycle rules.
Cost control guardrails: per-organization ingestion budget alerting and soft reject behavior when budget exceeded; documented defaults and override process.
End-to-end tests validate change-trace queries return accurate last-state within 2s for hot partitions and compaction jobs do not drop required fields.
Security review sign-off obtained and changes instrumented in audit console dashboards.
Non-prod rollout completed and perf impact <5% on ingest path; production rollout plan approved by SRE and Security teams.
implementation_notes: Ingest: add an enrichment stage in the audit-ingest consumer that looks up RBAC v2 delta payloads emitted by auth-service and attaches actor_role_snapshot and txn_id to the event metadata.
Kafka topic: use rbac-changes topic with compacted retention (cleanup.policy=compact) to keep canonical records of role bindings; consumer will join by subject_id to enrich audit events.

Compact index: new index template 'audit_rbac_compact_v1' with doc id = org|subject|resource; store last_seen_ts, last_change_txn, last_actor_id, and a circular buffer of up to 3 change summaries for quick forensics.
Compaction job: nightly Spark job to merge time-series audit events into compact index for partitions older than 24h; job writes with optimistic concurrency using txn_id to avoid races.
Partitioning: implement monthly rollover for cold partitions and leverage cloud lifecycle rules to move objects to archive storage class after 180 days.
Query path: add a lightweight API in console-backend to resolve change-trace via compact index, with fallback to raw time-series logs when deeper history is requested.
Backpressure: when compaction lag grows > 6h, switch ingest consumers to shedding mode where non-critical debug events are sampled to protect tail latency.
Cost controls: integrate with billing service to attribute index storage to org and emit alerts when forecasted spend exceeds threshold; default threshold = $500/month/org for audit indices.
Observability: add per-org compaction lag metrics, partition size, and query latency to existing audit dashboards.
comments: 2026-02-22: Kickoff meeting with Security, SRE, and Auth team. Agreed enrichment via rbac-changes Kafka topic is preferred to avoid blocking auth-service. Action: Auth to emit txn_id and actor_role_snapshot (Jordan).

2026-03-01: Design review — Security requested that compact index retain three recent changes rather than only last state to cover fast oscillation cases. Adjusted schema accordingly (see implementation_notes).
2026-03-05: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/auth/compare/PR-827 (emits rbac delta). Link in links.

2026-03-08: PoC compaction job ran in staging for 48h. Initial results: 42% index size reduction for orgs with noisy role churn; compaction job increased CPU by ~12% on worker nodes. Decision: tune Spark parallelism and add circuit breaker before prod rollout.
2026-03-12: Security review meeting — approved retention tiers but required that archived cold store be encrypted with customer-managed keys for enterprise orgs. Added to rollout plan.

2026-03-14: SRE flagged a potential race where concurrent admin updates could cause compaction to drop a transient change. Mitigation: include last_change_txn and use optimistic write with txn_id check.
test_plan: Unit tests for enrichment stage: simulated rbac-changes messages produce correct metadata fields in resulting audit events.
Integration test: pipeline from auth-service -> kafka -> ingest consumer -> compact index; validate document id mapping and fields.
Load test: seed high-frequency role churn (10k changes/min) in staging and measure compaction job lag and CPU/memory impact.
Forensic QA: run queries that reconstruct subject access timeline and compare compact index response vs raw-log-based reconstruction for 100 sample cases.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): deploy enrichment and compaction job to staging namespaces; run PoC for 72h and verify metrics.
Phase 2 (canary): enable for 5% of orgs flagged as low-risk; monitor compaction lag and query accuracy.
Phase 3 (gradual): increase to 50% with SRE runbook in place for backout; lock down archive lifecycle changes for enterprise orgs until KMS verified.
Phase 4 (global): full rollout with billing attribution and console features enabled.
risks: Compaction job could misapply merges during high-concurrency admin operations leading to missing transient changes.
Inaccurate enrichment if auth-service emits incomplete snapshots, causing compact index to reflect stale roles.
Storage cost mis-attribution could lead to billing disputes with customers if per-org tagging is incomplete.
Cold-store retrieval latency for deep forensic queries might be high and unexpected by customers.
mitigation: Use txn_id optimistic concurrency checks in compaction writes and keep a small circular buffer (3 changes) to cover races.
Add schema validation and a small delayed re-enrichment job that replays rbac-changes topic to fix missing snapshots.
Instrument per-org tags at ingest time and run a reconciliation job between billing records and actual index bytes weekly for 8 weeks post-rollout.
Expose expected cold retrieval SLAs in console and add an option for customers to extend hot retention for a fee.
estimated_cost_saving: $60k/year (projected) from index compaction and lifecycle policies at current ingestion levels
